key_insight: Agreement near equilibrium does not guarantee reliable fatigue dynamics: NequIP predicts much more plastic deformation than EAM under cyclic loading.
engineering_relevance: Interatomic potentials for fatigue simulation should be evaluated on driven, rare-event behavior, not only near-equilibrium properties.
method: Compare EAM and foundational NequIP potentials against reference near-equilibrium properties.
Apply fatigue cycling to a nanoscale flaw modeled after the Griffith crack problem.
evidence_signal: Both potentials closely match reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an intrinsic stacking fault energy about seven times lower than EAM, with the largest post-loading energy differences beyond thermally accessible ranges.
watch_item: Memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation are practical risks; comparison with EAM does not establish experimental accuracy.
paper_title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
